messages:
maria: kicking off a mini canary for cheshire-6b (int4) on prod-lite — 5% traffic, 6h window. need a quick cost vs quality sanity check before we ramp. details: seq=256, priming=3 shots, rerank off.
alex: quick Q — do we have baseline numbers from nova6b/int6 for the same slice?
ryan: baseline (nova6b int6, same slices): p50=85ms, p95=140ms, p99=260ms; throughput ~280 tok/s at seq256; cost ≈ $1.70 / 1k gen tokens (est).
ryan: cheshire-6b int4 smoke from staging (low qps): p50=78ms, p95=125ms, p99=210ms; throughput ~330 tok/s; cost ≈ $0.95 / 1k gen tokens.
sam: that's promising on latency + cost. any quality regressions on GTN dev prompts?
maria: initial automated eval (1000-shot mix): BLEU-ish style metric down 0.4 points, exact-match drop 0.7%; human subjective spot-check: rare factual hallucinations up ~0.2%.
jess: worth checking prompt-sensitivity slices — priming tokens can amplify quantization noise. recommend priming-rewrite test.
alex: product ask: if we save ~45% cost, what's the feature impact risk? product-lead: we can absorb a small perf regression if end-to-end UX unchanged; want rollback plan if task-specific recall drops >1.5%.
ryan: recommended smoke slices: search-query (concise), summarization (long-form), multi-turn chat (context carry). run A/B on these.
maria: schedule: run 6h canary, collect slice metrics + 4000 samples for each slice, then quick human review. if pass, move to 25% burst window.
ops-bot: canary deploy started by maria at 4343219900 — cluster: prod-lite-canary-3 — config: int4-quant, kvcache=on, batching=adaptive.
deploy-bot: canary healthcheck: initial 10m OK, error rate 0.1% (within threshold). :thumbsup:
alex: for unit econ calc — include the following: model cost per 1k tokens, expected tokens per request (median 120), cache hit assumptions (30%), and tail latency SLO impact.
sam: quick calc: at median 120 tok/request, cheshire cost ≈ $0.114/request, nova ≈ $0.204/request. with 30% cache hit effective cost cheshire ≈ $0.08, nova ≈ $0.143.
jess: also factor extra eval/ops cost for priming changes — small but not zero.
ryan: fallback plan idea: route 10% of canary failures (quality regressions or high-err slices) to nova6b int6; implement automatic rollback if slice-specific metric drops exceed thresholds for 15m.
product-lead: please add a quick user-impact note for GTN owners — want short summary for decisions by EOD.
maria: assigning tasks: @alex gather slice baselines (done by 4343220000), @sam run cost calc and scenario table, @jess run priming-sensitivity probe, @ryan wire up automated rollback triggers. I'll compile summary at end of canary.
alex: got it, starting slice runs now.
ryan: leaving a short checklist in this thread so we can copy into ops runbook: 1) start canary 5% 2) run smoke slices 3) collect 4k samples/slice 4) human QC on failure modes 5) evaluate unit econ table 6) decide ramp or rollback.
maria: perfect. ping me in thread with any anomalies. thanks team. :rocket:
